Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

violate verb

a woman: force or dishonour her

also rape (verb), deflower, ravish, force (a woman), seduce, dishonour

classical

Ter. Ad. 466–467: Fīliam ejus virginem vitiāvit.
Ter. Eun. 4.4.37: virginem (Lewis & Short)

vitiō, vitiāre, vitiāvī, vitiātum

verb, first conjugation

violate, deflower (a girl); in general spoil, corrupt

From vitium, a flaw.

Other words

  • comprimō, comprimere, compressī, compressum — lie with (a woman), usually by force

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Aul. 28: nam eam compressit dē summō adulēscēns locō; Liv. 1.4.2 (Lewis & Short)

    Literally press, hold down. The usual word in the prologues of comedy for the rape, often at a night festival, from which the plot starts.

  • stuprō, stuprāre, stuprāvī, stuprātum — dishonour by illicit sex: debauch, rape

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Aul. 36: quī illam stuprāvit noctū, Cereris vigiliīs; Cic. Fin. 2.66: Lucrētia vī stuprāta (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Fīliam ejus virginem vitiāvit.

    He violated his daughter, an unmarried girl.Ter. Ad. 466–467

  • isque hīc compressit virginem, adulēscentulus, vī, vīnulentus multā nocte in viā

    and here he forced a girl, a mere youth, by violence, drunk, late at night in the streetPlaut. Cist. 158–159

See also rape, debauchery, pregnant.

SourcesLewis & Short: vitio · Lewis & Short: comprimo · Lewis & Short: stupro

Plautus, Aulularia 28, 36; Cistellaria 158–159. Terence, Adelphoe 466–467.
